mnemonic.meaning: 到 arrive + 着 arrive: arrive, twice over. Arrival.
mnemonic.reading: You arrive, CHUCK off your shoes and wiggle your TOEs (とう・ちゃく).

examples.ja: 飛行機は予定より三十分早く到着した。
examples.en: The plane arrived thirty minutes earlier than scheduled.

items.note: 到着 = arrival. The opposite is 出発 (しゅっぱつ).

mnemonic.meaning: 徹 all the way through + 夜 night: through the whole night.
mnemonic.reading: てつ also means iron (鉄): an iron will to stay up all night. や as in 今夜 (tonight).

examples.ja: 試験の前の日に徹夜して勉強した。
examples.en: I stayed up all night studying the day before the exam.

items.note: 徹夜する = stay up all night. 夜 is や here (usually よる).

mnemonic.meaning: 引 pull + 越 cross over: pull your stuff across to a new home.
mnemonic.reading: The HICK loads everything into a COACH (ひっ・こし) and moves. From 引っ越す.

examples.ja: 来月、大阪へ引越しすることになった。
examples.en: It's been decided that I'm moving to Osaka next month.

items.note: Also written 引っ越し. The verb is 引っ越す.

mnemonic.meaning: 眺 has 目 (eye): you rest your eyes on the view.
mnemonic.reading: You gaze for a LONG time (長い, なが) at a MARE in the field (なが・める).

examples.ja: 窓から海を眺めるのが好きだ。
examples.en: I like looking out at the sea from the window.

items.note: 眺める = look at something for a while, like a view or the sky.

mnemonic.meaning: 握 has the hand radical 扌: grip it with your hand.
mnemonic.reading: Like にぎり sushi, rice squeezed in your hand. You grip with your KNEES (に) riding a horse.

examples.ja: 子どもは母親の手を強く握った。
examples.en: The child gripped his mother's hand tightly.

items.note: 握る = grip or squeeze. 握手 (あくしゅ) = handshake.

mnemonic.meaning: 溜 has 氵 (water): water pooling up. Things build up.
mnemonic.reading: EGGS (たまご) pile up in the fridge (たま・る).

examples.ja: 掃除しないと、部屋にほこりが溜まる。
examples.en: If you don't clean, dust builds up in the room.

items.note: 溜まる = something builds up. 溜める = you save it up.

mnemonic.meaning: Same kanji as 嫌い (dislike), which you know. This is the verb: to dislike.
mnemonic.reading: Take 嫌い (きらい), drop the い, add う: きらう.

examples.ja: 猫は水を嫌う。
examples.en: Cats dislike water.

items.note: 嫌う = dislike (verb). Everyday speech usually says 嫌いだ.

mnemonic.meaning: 一 one + 瞬 blink: one blink. An instant.
mnemonic.reading: いち + しゅん squeeze into いっしゅん, like 一緒 (いっしょ).

examples.ja: 一瞬、何が起きたのかわからなかった。
examples.en: For a moment, I didn't know what had happened.

items.note: 一瞬 = an instant. 瞬間 (しゅんかん) = the exact moment something happens.

mnemonic.meaning: 抱 is 扌 (hand) + 包 (wrap): wrap something in your arms. You can also hold problems or work.
mnemonic.reading: A kid hugs a big bag of CACAO (かかお) beans in their arms (かか・える).

examples.ja: 両手で荷物を抱えるのは大変だ。
examples.en: Carrying luggage in both arms is hard.

items.note: 抱える = hold in your arms; also to carry a burden. 問題を抱える = have problems.

mnemonic.meaning: 輝 has 光 (light): giving off light. Shining.
mnemonic.reading: A mirror (かがみ) that YAKs light everywhere (かが・やく): it sparkles.

examples.ja: 夜空に星が輝く。
examples.en: Stars shine in the night sky.

items.note: 輝く = shine brightly: stars, eyes, a future. 光る (ひかる) = give off light.

mnemonic.meaning: 願 wish, as in お願いします.
mnemonic.reading: Same as お願い (おねがい): the verb is 願う.

examples.ja: 家族の健康を願う。
examples.en: I wish for my family's health.

items.note: 願う = wish or hope. お願いします comes from this verb.

mnemonic.meaning: 今 now + 後 after: after now. From now on.
mnemonic.reading: こん as in 今度 (next time), ご as in 最後 (last).

examples.ja: 今後はもっと気をつけます。
examples.en: From now on, I'll be more careful.

items.note: 今後 = from now on (a bit formal). 今度 (こんど) = this time or next time.

mnemonic.meaning: 相 mutual + 当 fitting: fitting for the situation, and then some. Considerably.
mnemonic.reading: SO TOO much (そう・とう): considerably. そう as in 相談, とう as in 本当.

examples.ja: 彼は相当疲れているようだ。
examples.en: He seems quite tired.

items.note: 相当 = considerably, like かなり. It can also mean "equivalent to".

mnemonic.meaning: 超 has 走 (run): run beyond the line. Exceed.
mnemonic.reading: Same sound as 越える (cross over): you cross over the limit.

examples.ja: 今日の気温は三十五度を超えるそうだ。
examples.en: They say today's temperature will go over 35 degrees.

items.note: 超える = go over a limit or a number. 越える (same reading) = cross over a place.

mnemonic.meaning: 確 certain + 実 reality: a certain reality. Sure, reliable.
mnemonic.reading: かく as in 確認 (confirm), じつ as in 実は (level 1).

examples.ja: このままでは、遅刻するのは確実だ。
examples.en: At this rate, being late is certain.

items.note: 確実 = certain, sure. 確実に = definitely.

mnemonic.meaning: 当 that + 時 time: that time. Back then.
mnemonic.reading: とう as in 本当, じ as in 時間 (time).

examples.ja: 大学生だった当時、毎日アルバイトをしていた。
examples.en: Back when I was a university student, I worked part-time every day.

items.note: 当時 = back then, at a specific past time. 同時 (どうじ) = at the same time.

mnemonic.meaning: 成 become + 長 grow: become grown. Growth.
mnemonic.reading: せい as in 成功 (success), ちょう as in 社長 (company president): the president grows the company.

examples.ja: 子どもの成長は本当に早い。
examples.en: Children grow up so fast.

items.note: 成長する = grow up or develop (people, companies, the economy).

mnemonic.meaning: 中 middle + 心 heart: the heart of the middle. The center.
mnemonic.reading: ちゅう as in 中学 (middle school), しん as in 安心 (relief).

examples.ja: 駅は町の中心にある。
examples.en: The station is in the center of town.

items.note: 中心 = the middle or core of something. 〜を中心に = centered on.

mnemonic.meaning: MARU means "circle": the two things are so alike they come full circle. まるで〜のよう = just like.

examples.ja: 彼はまるで子供のように笑った。
examples.en: He laughed just like a child.

items.note: まるで〜ようだ / みたいだ = as if. With a negative it means "not at all": まるで分からない.

mnemonic.meaning: SHIKA + MO: "and on top of that, MOre!" It piles one fact on another.

examples.ja: この店は安い。しかも、おいしい。
examples.en: This place is cheap. And what's more, it's tasty.

items.note: Adds a stronger second point: 失敗した。しかも二回も。(I failed, and twice at that.) Also "and yet": 注意された。しかも、また同じ間違いをした。

mnemonic.meaning: 場 has 土 (earth): a patch of ground where something happens. A place or occasion.
mnemonic.reading: BA! You land on the spot. (ば) Same ば as 場所 and 会場.

examples.ja: その場ですぐに返事をした。
examples.en: I replied right there on the spot.

items.note: Common in set phrases: その場で (on the spot), 場合 (case). On its own, ば is a bit formal; 場所 is the everyday word.

mnemonic.meaning: SORE + SORE: "that one, and that one". Each thing taken one by one.

examples.ja: 人にはそれぞれ好みがある。
examples.en: Everyone has their own tastes.

items.note: Often 〜はそれぞれ違う: each one is different. Close to 各自 (かくじ) but more everyday.

mnemonic.meaning: NAN = what, TOKA = or something. "Somehow or other" you get through.

examples.ja: なんとか終電に間に合った。
examples.en: I somehow made the last train.

items.note: なんとかする = do something about it. なんとかなる = it'll work out somehow.

mnemonic.meaning: 件 = 亻 (person) + 牛 (cow). A person arguing about a cow: a matter to deal with.
mnemonic.reading: KEN, your coworker, handles every case. (けん)

examples.ja: その件については、後で話しましょう。
examples.en: Let's talk about that matter later.

items.note: Used a lot at work: この件 (this matter). As a counter it counts cases or emails: 3件.

mnemonic.meaning: 例 = 亻 (person) + 列 (line): a person at the front of the line, setting the example.
mnemonic.reading: RAY points to an example on the board. (れい) Same れい as 例えば.

examples.ja: 例を挙げて説明してください。
examples.en: Please explain with an example.

items.note: 例の + noun = "that ... we talked about": 例の件 (that matter).

mnemonic.meaning: IZURE sounds like "is your..." turn coming? Sooner or later, it will.

examples.ja: いずれ分かる日が来るよ。
examples.en: The day will come when you understand, sooner or later.

items.note: いずれにしても = in any case. いずれ also means "either one" in formal speech.

mnemonic.meaning: MASA + NI: think "MASter-ly" precise. Exactly that, no more, no less.

examples.ja: これはまさに私が探していた本だ。
examples.en: This is exactly the book I was looking for.

items.note: Stronger than ちょうど. Often for emphasis: まさにその通り = exactly right.

mnemonic.meaning: HOBO: a hobo who has almost everything packed. Almost, nearly.

examples.ja: 仕事はほぼ終わった。
examples.en: The work is almost finished.

items.note: A little more formal than だいたい. Common in news: ほぼ毎日 (almost every day).

mnemonic.meaning: 一 one + 方 direction: one direction, while the other goes elsewhere. On the other hand.
mnemonic.reading: IPPO: one step (一歩) to one side. (いっぽう)

examples.ja: 兄は背が高い。一方、弟は小さい。
examples.en: The older brother is tall. The younger one, on the other hand, is small.

items.note: Also the grammar 〜一方だ (keeps getting more and more).

mnemonic.meaning: 流 has 氵 (water): water that keeps moving. A flow or current.
mnemonic.reading: The river flows NAGAREly along... NAGA (long) + RE: a long stream. (ながれ)

examples.ja: 川の流れが速い。
examples.en: The river's current is fast.

items.note: Also used for the flow of time or events: 話の流れ (the flow of a conversation).
